elements.quote: Systematic review registration: PROSPERO CRD42020188168.
elements.reason: The abstract identifies the report as a systematic review via its registration statement and describes a living review critically appraising data.

elements.quote: Purpose: This living review aims to critically appraise available data about secondary attack rates from people with asymptomatic, pre-symptomatic and symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection.
elements.reason: Explicit objective/review question stated in the Purpose section of the abstract.

elements.quote: Study selection: Studies that report on contact tracing of index cases with SARS-CoV-2 infection in either English or Chinese were included.
elements.reason: Main inclusion criteria (and implicitly exclusions) are specified in the abstract.

elements.quote: Data sources: Medline, EMBASE, China Academic Journals full-text database (CNKI), and pre-print servers were searched from 30 December 2019 to 3 July 2020 using relevant MESH terms.
elements.reason: Information sources and the date of last search are reported.

elements.quote: Two authors independently extracted data and assessed study quality and risk of bias.
elements.reason: Risk of bias assessment is mentioned but the specific tool/method is not named in the abstract.

elements.quote: We calculated the secondary attack rate as the number of contacts with SARS-CoV-2, divided by the number of contacts tested.
elements.reason: Methods of synthesis (calculation of secondary attack rates and summary estimates) are described under Data extraction/Data synthesis.

elements.quote: Of 927 studies identi fi ed, 80 were included.
elements.reason: Total number of included studies is reported, but the number of participants and study characteristics are not summarized in the abstract.

elements.quote: Summary secondary attack rate estimates were 1% (95% CI 0% e 2%) ... for asymptomatic index cases in ten studies, 7% (95% CI 3% e 11%) ... for pre-symptomatic cases in 11 studies and 6% (95% CI 5% e 8%) ... for symptomatic index cases in 40 studies.
elements.reason: Main outcome results are reported with number of studies per outcome.

elements.quote: Summary secondary attack rate estimates were 1% (95% CI 0% e 2%) with a prediction interval of 0% e 10% for asymptomatic index cases in ten studies
elements.reason: Meta-analysis summary estimates with confidence intervals (and prediction intervals) are reported.

elements.quote: Asymptomatic patients can transmit SARS-CoV-2 to others, but our fi ndings indicate that such individuals are responsible for fewer secondary infections than people with symptoms.
elements.reason: Direction of effect and favored group (symptomatic transmit more) are indicated.

elements.quote: Limitations: We excluded some studies because the index case or number of contacts were unclear.
elements.reason: A brief limitations statement is included in the abstract, though limited in depth.

elements.quote: Conclusion: Asymptomatic patients can transmit SARS-CoV-2 to others, but our fi ndings indicate that such individuals are responsible for fewer secondary infections than people with symptoms.
elements.reason: General interpretation and public health implication of results are provided.
No funding source for the review is stated in the abstract.

elements.quote: Systematic review registration: PROSPERO CRD42020188168.
elements.reason: Register name (PROSPERO) and registration number are provided in the abstract.

elements.quote: Reports suggest that asymptomatic individuals (those with no symptoms at all throughout infection) with severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) are infectious, but the extent of transmission based on symptom status requires further study.
elements.reason: The abstract Background briefly indicates current knowledge and the uncertainty, but no full Introduction/rationale text was retrieved, so the description of existing knowledge and uncertainties is only partial.

elements.quote: the extent of transmission based on symptom status requires further study. Purpose: This living review aims to critically appraise available data about secondary attack rates from people with asymptomatic, pre-symptomatic and symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection.
elements.reason: The need for the review is implied by the stated gap and purpose in the abstract, but no fuller Introduction rationale was available in the retrieved evidence.
No retrieved evidence cites prior similar systematic reviews or explains the need for this review relative to them, despite it being a living (potentially updating) review.
This is a review of transmission (secondary attack rates), not of intervention effects, so a mechanism of action does not apply.
No complex intervention is evaluated, so a logic model is not applicable.

elements.quote: The aim of this review is to summarize the available evidence about secondary attack rates (defined as the probability that an infected individual will transmit the disease to a susceptible individual) among the contacts of individuals with SARS-CoV-2 with different symptom status to provide information about how contagious they are, and their role in driving the pandemic.
elements.reason: The Introduction ends with an explicit objective statement, and the abstract's Purpose section restates it ('This living review aims to critically appraise available data about secondary attack rates from people with asymptomatic, pre-symptomatic and symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection.'), clearly defining the review question including the population (contacts of index cases), exposure (symptom status), and outcome (secondary attack rate).

This is a review of transmission/secondary attack rates in observational outbreak and contact-tracing studies, not a review of intervention effects, so formal PICO-stated planned comparisons do not apply.

elements.quote: Studies were eligible if they met the inclusion criteria: (a) report on COVID-19 or SARS-CoV-2 infection and (b) report an outbreak investigation or contact tracing study. Exclusion criteria were: (a) review articles; (b) observational studies providing only the proportion of individuals infected; (c) studies that do not indicate the number of contacts or secondary infections; and (d) reports in media sources.
elements.reason: Eligible topic and study designs (outbreak investigations, contact tracing studies) are specified, but settings and follow-up requirements are not stated as eligibility criteria.

elements.quote: (d) reports in media sources
elements.reason: Publication status is partially addressed (media reports excluded; the flow diagram in text_16/figure_3 also shows exclusions for 'Retracted' and 'Not a prepint or published'), but no language or dissemination-year restrictions are reported.

elements.quote: Media report 1 Retracted 1 Modeling study 1 No testing for contacts 1 Analysis on partial contacts 1 Not a prepint or published 2 Provides prevalence 22 Duplicate 25 No clear denominator 53
elements.reason: The flow diagram distinguishes some exclusion reasons (e.g., 'No testing for contacts' vs 'No clear denominator'), but it does not explicitly separate exclusion because outcomes were not measured from exclusion because outcome results were not reported.

elements.quote: A pooled analysis was carried out to generate summary estimates for the secondary attack rate in each subgroup analysed (asymptomatic, pre-symptomatic and symptomatic index cases)
elements.reason: Synthesis groups are specified (asymptomatic, pre-symptomatic, symptomatic index cases) and correspond to the review objective of estimating secondary attack rate by symptom status (text_5).
No rationale is provided for notable eligibility restrictions such as excluding review articles, studies without contact numbers, or media reports.

elements.quote: The initial search was completed from 30 December 2019 to 21 May 2020, searches were repeated on 8 June 2020 and 3 July 2020, owing to the rapidly increasing number of studies.
elements.reason: The dates of the initial and repeat (last) searches of the databases are explicitly reported.

elements.quote: systematic searches of eight databases: Medline, EMBASE, Europe PMC, Web of Science, SCOPUS, Chinese database (CNKI), and preprint servers (MedRxiv, BioRxiv)
elements.reason: Database names are reported, but the search interface/platform and coverage dates for each database are not specified.
No study registers, regulatory databases, or online repositories (beyond preprint servers, covered under databases) are reported as searched.
No websites, search engines, or other online sources are reported as searched.
No organisations or manufacturers are reported as contacted to identify studies.

elements.quote: We also manually screened the references of the included original studies and reviews to identify additional eligible studies.
elements.reason: The types of reference lists examined (included original studies and reviews) are specified.

No journals or conference proceedings were separately consulted as sources.

elements.quote: From each study, the following variables were extracted: the name of the fi rst author, year of publication, country, sample size, details of index cases (categorized as asymptomatic, pre-symptomatic and symptomatic); event details such as environment, transmission details; number of contacts, number of secondary cases.
elements.reason: Data items sought are listed in the extraction variables (text_9), and key definitions are provided in text_6 ('Secondary attack rate was de fi ned as the number of new SARS-CoV-2 infection cases among susceptible contacts of primary cases divided by the total number of susceptible contacts'), but the outcome domains are not formally presented as a defined list of outcomes with explicit definitions for each domain.

No time frame of measurement for the outcome domains (e.g. follow-up duration for secondary attack rate) is specified in the Methods; the 14-day follow-up is mentioned only in the quality assessment section (text_16) as a study quality criterion, not as a specified outcome measurement time frame.

elements.quote: Secondary attack rates were computed from raw data in each study... A pooled analysis was carried out to generate summary estimates for the secondary attack rate in each subgroup analysed (asymptomatic, pre-symptomatic and symptomatic index cases), in the framework of a random effect model. The Freeman e Tukey double-arcsine variance-stabilizing transformation was used to combine data... Secondary attack rates are presented as a proportion along with 95% CIs in forest plots.
elements.reason: The effect measure (secondary attack rate as a proportion with 95% CI, pooled under a random-effects model using the Freeman-Tukey double-arcsine transformation) is clearly specified for all outcomes.

elements.quote: an I 2 value above 75% indicates high heterogeneity
elements.reason: No thresholds or ranges for interpreting the size of the effect (secondary attack rate) are reported; the only threshold given concerns heterogeneity (I2), not effect size interpretation.
The manuscript reports no re-expression of synthesized results into another effect measure; results are presented only as secondary attack rates, so this conditional requirement does not apply.

elements.quote: The Freeman e Tukey double-arcsine variance-stabilizing transformation was used to combine data, because of its advantage over log and logit transformations, which do not allow computation of the proportion in the presence of zero event counts
elements.reason: A rationale is given for the choice of transformation method, but no explicit justification is provided for the choice of the secondary attack rate itself as the effect measure.

elements.quote: among those weidenti fi ed 69 studies that indicated the symptom status of index case(s). In this analysis, we excluded 11 studies that reported asymptomatic and symptomatic index cases together or in which no symptom status of the index case was available. We re-classi fi ed three studies from asymptomatic to pre-symptomatic as the index cases developed symptoms later during the disease course after reviewing the details and contacting the authors [19 e 21].
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly describes the process used to decide which studies were eligible for the synthesis (the pooled secondary attack rate analysis by symptom status): of the 80 included studies, 69 indicating index-case symptom status were selected for the analysis, 11 with mixed or unavailable symptom status were excluded, and three studies were re-classified after reviewing details and contacting authors. This grouping process is further supported by text_9, where index cases were categorized as asymptomatic, pre-symptomatic, and symptomatic during data extraction. Although the description appears in the Results section rather than Methods, the process for synthesis eligibility is clearly reported.

elements.quote: Secondary attack rates were computed from raw data in each study, dividing the number of infected contacts of primary cases by the total number of susceptible exposed contacts. ... The Freeman e Tukey double-arcsine variancestabilizing transformation was used to combine data, because of its advantage over log and logit transformations, which do not allow computation of the proportion in the presence of zero event counts
elements.reason: The manuscript describes data preparation methods for synthesis: computing secondary attack rates from raw counts and applying the Freeman-Tukey double-arcsine transformation to handle zero event counts, plus pooling in a random effects model. Handling of missing summary statistics is partially addressed in text_9 (contacting authors when data were not reported), but the core data preparation/conversion methods are clearly described.

elements.quote: The studies are summarized in text and table form, descriptive statistics were completed for key outcome measures.
